task:
A top-level scalar added to a document can silently move into a table.

Start with doc = parse('a.b = 1\n'). Run doc['a']['c'] = {} and then doc['z'] = 2. The document now renders z after a [a.c] header, so z re-parses as a.c.z. A scalar set on the document must stay at the top level, ahead of any table header.

For that example, doc.as_string() must be exactly:

z = 2

a.b = 1

[a.c]

with a trailing newline after [a.c], and parse(doc.as_string()) must equal {'z': 2, 'a': {'b': 1, 'c': {}}}.

The same must hold however deep the header sits: any dotted-key entry that renders a table header or an array of tables, directly or through nested dotted keys, counts.

A dotted key that renders only inline must not change. After doc = parse('a.b = 1\n') and doc['z'] = 2, doc.as_string() must be 'a.b = 1\nz = 2\n'.

Everything else must keep working.
